the ventral and dorsal streams are separate, and that they are specialized for perceptual and motor functions respectively.

the ventral and dorsal streams of visual projections from primary visual cortex are differentially involved in the identification and recognition of objects and the control of actions directed at those objects.

the ventral and dorsal streams of projections from the primary visual cortex to the temporal lobe and to the posterior pariental cortex, respectively, are functionally dissociated, with the former mediating object recognition and the latter visually guided action.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms that underlie the perception and control of visually guided actions.
the functional organization of the primate visual system, particularly with regard to the role of the ventral and dorsal visual pathways in the control of visually guided action.
the neural mechanisms of visual perception and action, and the relationship between them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are two separate and distinct pathways in the visual system.

the dorsal and ventral streams are not functionally equivalent and that they are functionally distinct in that the dorsal stream is concerned with the visual guidance of action, while the ventral stream is concerned with object recognition.
the ventral visual pathway is involved in the identification of objects and the dorsal pathway is concerned with the visual control of movements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

perception and action have separate visual pathways, which are functionally specialized and anatomically distinct, and that the visual system is not a single entity but rather a set of specialized systems that operate in parallel.
the visual system has two separate pathways that are responsible for two distinct functions, perception and action.
the ventral and the dorsal visual streams have different functions, and the two streams are functionally independent of each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
perception and action are mediated by different visual streams.
there is no need for a single, unitary, object representation that can be used both for perception and action.
the ventral and dorsal streams are functionally specialized for different types of visual processing, and this is reflected in their differential vulnerability to damage.
